notes: Spec asserts: ready → working → waiting when the assistant's reply ends in a clarifying question and the recipe deliberately stops there (no reply sent, no tool call). This is the trailing-? plain-question-to-the-user path (session.IsWaitingForUserInput → state_classifier.go decision 2a, fed by ProseIndicatesWaiting over the assistant_message_committed text) — NOT muse's separate kind:"approval" permission-prompt flow, which a different cell covers. Single-birth session model (muse's session id = directory basename, fixed at session start), so the birth phase anchors to "start" unpinned. The recipe's prompt explicitly forbids tool use: muse's system prompt otherwise steers the model toward its dedicated request_user_input tool for blocking questions, which the daemon does not currently recognize as user-blocking (see the cell's caveats) — live-confirmed on this machine that the explicit no-tools instruction reliably produces a plain-text reply ending '?' instead. Per the claudecode/mistral-vibe sibling specs for this scenario, only the ready→working→waiting half is driven; the resume half (waiting→working→ready) is intentionally out of scope for this recipe. CORRECTED at record time: observations.cost_nonzero true->false -- muse-spark-1.3-contributor has no pricing-catalog entry in core/pkg/capacity, so a muse session genuinely prices at $0 (same reasoning already applied in the 5-1_token-accounting and 1-8_model-context-display sibling cells); also pinned turn_start/turn_end_waiting with same_session_as:session_birth per the batch-1 vacuous-pass fix (subagent-turn misattribution).
